# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop — additional management features]
- Approved scenarios: [12]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

Scenario ID: SCN-013
Title: Delete a bookmark with a brief undo, then permanent
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

Each bookmark has a **Delete** action. Deleting removes the item immediately and
shows a bottom **undo bar** ("Deleted … — Undo") for a few seconds; clicking Undo
restores the item to where it was. Once the undo period ends, the deletion is
**permanent**. This is distinct from archiving: archiving keeps the item, delete
removes it for good after the grace period.

## Gherkin
Feature: Delete a bookmark

  Scenario: Delete with undo
    Given a bookmark is shown
    When the user deletes it
    Then it is removed from the list immediately
    And an undo bar is shown for a few seconds
    And clicking Undo within that time restores the bookmark

  Scenario: Deletion becomes permanent
    Given a bookmark was deleted
    When the undo period elapses without Undo
    Then the bookmark is permanently removed

## Assumptions
- Deletion is quick (no confirmation prompt); safety comes from the undo window.
- After the undo window, there is no further recovery.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-005 (archive is the "keep it" alternative)

Scenario ID: SCN-014
Title: Change a bookmark's saved URL, optionally refreshing details
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

In a bookmark's edit panel there is a **Link (URL)** field so the saved address
can be changed. Alongside it is an **optional** choice: "Update title, description
& preview from this link." When the URL is changed and that option is selected,
the automatic details are re-gathered from the new link; when it is not selected,
the user's existing title/description/wording are kept as-is. The choice is made
each time (not always, not never), because sometimes the user wants the fresh page
details and sometimes wants to keep their own wording.

## Gherkin
Feature: Change a saved URL

  Scenario: Change URL and refresh details
    Given the user is editing a bookmark
    When the user changes the Link (URL) and chooses to update details from it
    And presses Done
    Then the bookmark's address is updated
    And its title, description and preview are re-gathered from the new link

  Scenario: Change URL and keep existing wording
    Given the user is editing a bookmark
    When the user changes the Link (URL) and does not choose to update details
    And presses Done
    Then the bookmark's address is updated
    And its existing title, description and note are unchanged

## Assumptions
- The refresh option only takes effect when the URL actually changed.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-011 (edit title/description), SCN-001 (auto details)

- **"Mark read"** in the bar means *turn off* the read-later flag for the selected items (the counterpart to "Read later"). Does that pairing make sense to you?
- **Selection stays within the current view/filter** — "Select all in view" never reaches beyond what you're currently looking at. Is scoping bulk actions to the filtered view what you'd expect (so you can, say, filter to a tag and act on exactly those)?

    And no bookmarks outside the current view/filter are selected

  Scenario: Clear the selection
    When the user chooses Clear
    Then no bookmarks are selected and the bulk bar is hidden

## Assumptions
- Selection scope never reaches beyond the current view/filter.

- SCN-017 (bulk actions), SCN-006 (filter), SCN-004/005 (views)

Scenario ID: SCN-017
Title: Act on selected bookmarks together (tag, read/unread, archive, delete)
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

With one or more bookmarks selected, the bulk action bar can:
- **Add a tag to all** selected (with suggestions from existing tags; existing
  tags on an item are not duplicated).
- **Remove a tag from all** selected — the remove box **suggests only tags that
  are actually present on the selected bookmarks**, which makes removal clear and
  avoids mistakes.
- **Mark read later** (flag all) and **Mark read** (turn the flag off for all) —
  a clear pair.
- **Archive** all selected.
- **Delete** all selected, with a **single undo** covering the whole batch.

## Gherkin
Feature: Bulk actions on selected bookmarks

  Scenario: Add a tag to all selected
    Given several bookmarks are selected
    When the user adds a tag in the bulk bar
    Then that tag is added to every selected bookmark (no duplicates)

  Scenario: Remove a tag from all selected
    Given several bookmarks are selected
    When the user opens the remove-tag box
    Then only tags present on the selected bookmarks are suggested
    And choosing one removes it from every selected bookmark that has it

  Scenario: Mark read-later / read for all selected
    When the user chooses "Read later" then "Mark read"
    Then all selected bookmarks are flagged, then unflagged

  Scenario: Archive all selected
    When the user archives the selection
    Then every selected bookmark is archived

  Scenario: Delete all selected with one undo
    When the user deletes the selection
    Then all selected bookmarks are removed
    And a single undo restores the whole batch within the grace period

## Assumptions
- Remove-tag suggestions are scoped to tags on the selected items.
- Bulk delete shares the same undo-then-permanent model as single delete.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-016 (selection), SCN-002/003 (tags), SCN-004 (read later),
  SCN-005 (archive), SCN-013 (delete/undo)

Saved searches work. Open http://maker:4001/saved-search.html — there's a **"Saved searches"** strip under the tabs (I pre-seeded two examples) and a **"★ Save this search"** button under the search area.

**Please try:**

1. **Use a saved search.** Click the **"Dev reference"** chip in the strip. → It instantly applies its query (`#dev AND #reference`) and shows the matching bookmarks; the chip highlights as active. Now click **"Reading — to read"** → it switches to the **To read** view filtered to the `reading` tag. So one click re-runs a whole search.

2. **Save your own.** Click the **All** tab, then type `#design` in the search box. The **"★ Save this search"** button lights up (with the note "Saves the current text, tag filter and view together"). Click it, give it a name like `Design links`, and press Save → it appears as a new chip you can reuse.

3. **Remove one.** Click the small **×** on any saved-search chip to delete it.

Two decisions to confirm:
- A saved search **captures the whole combination** — the text query, the active tag filter, *and* the current view (All/To read/Archived) — not just the text. Is bundling all three what you want, or would you rather it remember only the text query?
- The **Save button is disabled** when there's nothing to save (empty search, no filter, default view) or when the exact search is already saved, so you can't make duplicates. Reasonable?

And one to note: this screen doesn't include the **sort order** in a saved search (sort lives on the main list). Would you want a saved search to also remember the sort, or is sort separate in your mind?

Scenario ID: SCN-018
Title: Save and reuse named searches (query + tag filter + view)
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

The user can save the current search as a named, reusable saved search. A saved
search **captures the whole combination**: the text query, the active tag filter,
and the current view (All / To read / Archived) — this is what makes it a reusable
filter rather than just saved text. Saved searches appear as chips; clicking one
re-applies its whole combination at once and highlights it as active; a small ×
removes it.

The **Save** action is disabled when there is nothing to save (empty query, no
tag filter, default view) or when the exact same combination is already saved, so
duplicates and empty saves are prevented.

**Sort order is deliberately NOT part of a saved search** — sorting stays
independent so the user can reorder results without changing the saved search.

## Gherkin
Feature: Saved searches

  Scenario: Apply a saved search
    Given a saved search exists
    When the user clicks it
    Then its text query, tag filter and view are all applied together
    And it is highlighted as the active saved search

  Scenario: Save the current search
    Given the current search has a query, tag filter, or non-default view
    And the same combination is not already saved
    When the user saves it and gives it a name
    Then it appears as a reusable saved search

  Scenario: Prevent empty or duplicate saves
    Given the current search is empty (default) or identical to an existing saved search
    Then the Save action is unavailable

  Scenario: Remove a saved search
    When the user removes a saved search
    Then it no longer appears

  Scenario: Sorting is independent of saved searches
    Given a saved search is applied
    When the user changes the sort order
    Then the saved search itself is unchanged

## Assumptions
- Captured criteria: text query + tag filter + view (not sort).
- Names are user-provided (with a suggested default).

## Related scenarios
- SCN-006 (tag filter), SCN-007 (search), SCN-015 (sort, kept separate)

content.text:
Snapshot works. Open http://maker:4001/snapshot.html — the **"CSS Grid"** item already has a preserved copy (green **"📄 Copy saved"** badge); others don't yet.

**Please try:**
1. **View a preserved copy.** On the "CSS Grid" item, click **📄 View copy**. → An overlay opens showing the **saved, read-only version of the page** — its text is kept so you could still read it even if the original vanished. Close it with × or by clicking outside.
2. **Preserve a page yourself.** On another item, click **📄 Save a copy**. After a moment it shows "Saving a copy…" then gains the **green badge** and now offers **View copy** and **↻ Update copy**.

Now the decisions that shape this feature — I built it one way but want your call:

- **When should a copy be made?** Right now it's **manual** — you click "Save a copy" on the ones you care about. The alternatives are: **automatically preserve a copy of every bookmark** when you save it, or a **default that you can turn on/off** (auto for everything, but still manual control per item). Which fits how you'd use this? (Auto keeps everything safe but stores far more; manual keeps it lightweight and deliberate.)

- **What should the copy preserve?** I simulated a **readable text version** of the page (the words/article, stripped of clutter). The alternative is trying to keep the **full visual page** (layout and images as it looked). For guarding against link rot, which matters more to you — the readable content, or the exact appearance?

- And is a **read-only saved copy plus an "Update copy" option** (to re-capture if the page changed) the right level of control?

content:
I’d prefer automatic saving as a setting that I can turn on or off, while still keeping the per-bookmark manual controls.

For the copy itself, I want the full page preserved as a self-contained file, including its layout and images, rather than only extracted text. If the link is a PDF, save the PDF itself. Read-only viewing plus “Update copy” is the right control.

I’d also like an option to preserve a bookmark through the Internet Archive as another safeguard.

<system-reminder>
# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.
</system-reminder>

Title: Preserve a full-page copy of a bookmark (manual or automatic)
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

A bookmark can have a preserved **full-page copy** stored as a **self-contained
file** that keeps the page's **layout and images** (not just extracted text), so
the content survives if the original later changes or goes offline. If the link
is a **PDF**, the **original PDF file** is preserved in its native format rather
than converted to a web page.

Control:
- **Automatic saving is a setting** the user can turn **on or off**: when on, a
  full-page copy is saved automatically for every new bookmark.
- **Per-bookmark manual controls remain** regardless of the setting: "Save a
  copy" when none exists, and "View copy" / "Update copy" when one does.
- Viewing a copy is **read-only**; "Update copy" re-captures the current page.
- A bookmark with a copy shows a "Copy saved" indicator.

    Given a bookmark has no copy
    When the user chooses "Save a copy"
    Then a full-page copy (layout and images) is preserved
    And the bookmark shows a "Copy saved" indicator with View / Update actions

  Scenario: Preserve a PDF in its original format
    Given a bookmark's link is a PDF
    When a copy is saved
    Then the original PDF file is preserved (not converted to a web page)

  Scenario: Automatic copy setting
    Given the "automatically save a copy" setting is on
    When the user saves a new bookmark
    Then a full-page copy is preserved automatically

  Scenario: Setting off keeps manual control
    Given the automatic setting is off
    Then no automatic copy is made
    And the user can still save or update a copy per bookmark

  Scenario: View is read-only; update re-captures
    Given a bookmark has a copy
    When the user views it
    Then it opens read-only
    And "Update copy" re-captures the page

## Assumptions
- A copy is a self-contained file preserving layout + images; PDFs kept as PDF.
- The automatic-save toggle is a user setting (also see display preferences).

## Related scenarios
- SCN-020 (Internet Archive, independent safeguard), SCN-001 (save)

**Please try each — they apply instantly behind the panel:**

4. **Open to:** choose **To read** → sets which view the app opens on.
5. **Default sort:** choose **Title A–Z** → sets the starting sort order (the list's Sort control updates to match).
6. **Automatically save a full-page copy:** the on/off setting for the page-preservation feature lives here too, alongside the other defaults.

The set of preferences I included: **appearance/theme, list density, show-or-hide previews, which view to open on, default sort order, and auto-save copies.**

Title: Show bookmarks in pages with a chosen page size
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved

## Approved behaviour

The list shows a chosen number of bookmarks per page (5 / 10 / 25 / 50 / All).
When there are more results than the page size, a **"Showing X–Y of N"** count and
**Prev / Next** paging controls appear; when everything fits (or "All" is chosen),
no pager is shown. Paging works together with the current view, filters and sort.
If the current page falls out of range (e.g. after deleting items), it is clamped
to a valid page.

## Gherkin
Feature: Paged list

  Scenario: Page through results
    Given there are more bookmarks than the page size
    Then only one page is shown at a time with a count and Prev/Next controls
    And Next/Prev move between pages

  Scenario: All on one page
    When the page size is "All" (or results fit in one page)
    Then no pager is shown

  Scenario: Page clamped after changes
    Given the user is on the last page
    When items are removed so fewer pages remain
    Then the shown page is clamped to a valid page

## Assumptions
- Page size is a display preference (SCN-023).
- Paging applies after view/filter/sort.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-023 (preferences), SCN-015 (sort), SCN-006/007 (filter/search)

We've settled all the management features you asked for. Before I propose building, let me close the **edge cases** for them — a couple worth seeing, the rest quick confirmations.

**Please try these two on** http://maker:4001/import-export.html:
1. **A file that isn't bookmarks.** Click **⬆ Import** — rather than choosing a file, I'll note that if you pick a non-bookmarks or empty file, you get a clear **"No bookmarks were found in that file"** message instead of an empty import. (You can trigger the redundant-file case next.)
2. **Importing things you already have.** Click **⬆ Import → "Use a sample export" → Import** once. Then do **⬆ Import → "Use a sample export"** *again* → the preview now shows **"All 5 already saved"** and the Import button is disabled, so re-importing never creates duplicates.

And a few edge behaviors I'd rather confirm in words than stage (they depend on timing or outside services):
- **Delete is recoverable only briefly** — after the undo bar disappears, a deleted bookmark (single or a bulk batch) is permanently gone. Good?
- **If preserving a copy fails** (page unreachable) or **the Internet Archive is unavailable**, the app tells you it couldn't do it, leaves the bookmark otherwise intact, and lets you try again later — rather than failing the whole save. Right approach?
- **Exporting with nothing saved** still gives you a valid (empty) file. Fine?
- **A saved search whose tag you later delete** simply shows a clean "no matches" rather than breaking. OK?

If those all sound right, I think we've fully covered the functionality and its edges — and I'd be ready to propose moving from exploration into building the real app.

Title: Notes support Markdown, displayed formatted
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved

Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

A bookmark's note is written and edited as **Markdown** and **displayed
formatted** when viewing. Supported formatting includes headings, bold, italic,
inline code and code blocks, bullet and numbered lists, links, and block quotes.
Editing a note returns the **raw Markdown** to change (not the formatted view).
Text that is not valid Markdown simply appears as plain text. For safety, any
raw HTML pasted into a note is shown as **text, not executed**, and only
http/https links become clickable.

## Gherkin
Feature: Markdown notes

    Given a note contains Markdown
    When the bookmark is viewed
    Then the note is shown with the Markdown rendered (headings, bold, italic, lists, links, code, quotes)

  Scenario: Edit returns raw Markdown
    Given a note is shown formatted
    When the user edits it
    Then the raw Markdown text is presented for editing

  Scenario: Plain text stays plain
    Given a note has no Markdown syntax
    Then it is shown as plain text

  Scenario: HTML is not executed
    Given a note contains raw HTML
    Then the HTML is shown as text and not executed
    And only http/https links are made clickable

## Assumptions
- A safe subset of Markdown is supported; unknown syntax renders as text.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-002 (add note), SCN-003 (edit note)

That's the last piece. Here's everything we've settled together, in plain terms — this is the scope I'd build.

**Saving & automatic details**
- Paste a link and save it in one step; it appears at the top of your list.
- The title, description, site icon, and a preview image (when the page has one) are filled in automatically. If a page's details can't be read, the link is still saved and you can type them in yourself.

**Organizing**
- Add tags and a note while saving (both optional), with suggestions from tags you already use and an easy way to create new ones.
- Edit a bookmark's title, description, tags, note, or even its link later — changing the link can optionally refresh the details.
- Notes are written in Markdown and shown nicely formatted.

**Keeping the list useful**
- Mark things "Read later" and see just those; archive links to keep them without cluttering the main list; restore or delete (with a brief undo) as needed.
- Three views — All, To read, Archived — each with a count.
- Sort by newest, oldest, title, or recently updated.

**Finding again**
- A powerful search across title, description, note, tags, and link — with exact phrases, tag-specific searches, and AND/OR/NOT with grouping — plus a tag filter bar. Save any search (query + filter + view) to reuse with one click.

**Working in bulk**
- Select several bookmarks, or everything in the current view, to tag, untag, mark read/unread, archive, or delete together.

**Keeping copies safe**
- Preserve a full-page copy of a bookmark (kept as a self-contained file; PDFs kept as PDFs), automatically or on demand, and optionally also save it to the Internet Archive.

**Moving in and out**
- Import your browser's bookmarks (folders become tags, duplicates skipped, original titles/dates/tags preserved) and export as a browser file or a full backup.

**Comfort**
- Display preferences: light/dark/match-system, density, text size, show/hide previews, how many per page (with paging), which view to open on, and default sort.

It's a personal, single-user web app, and we've walked through the empty, error, overflow, and duplicate situations for these along the way.

**May I start building this scope now?** Once you approve, I'll switch into development and implement exactly what we've confirmed here.

# Acceptance

Phase 4. Present the result to the user and obtain acceptance confirmation.

---

## Acceptance procedure

### Presenting the result

Present the implemented software to the client and report that verification
against the approved scenarios' GWT specifications and the internal tests has
passed. Summarise the verification outcome in plain language and provide access
to the implemented software.

For the first cycle, the report covers all approved scenarios. For later cycles,
it covers the changed scenarios and affected existing scenarios.

### Acceptance confirmation

Ask the client to accept the implemented software as a whole on the basis of
the approved behaviour and the verification report. Acceptance completes the
development work for the cycle.

### Handling client requests

Use the requirement scenarios approved during Phase 1 as the baseline. Classify
each request by whether fulfilling it changes that baseline:

- Implementation error: the implementation does not satisfy an approved
  scenario. Return to Phase 2, fix the implementation, repeat verification in
  Phase 3, and request acceptance again. Preserve the approved scenario.
- Requirement change or addition: fulfilling the request requires changing an
  approved scenario or adding a scenario. Record the request for the next cycle
  in context/session-log.md, retaining the current approved scenarios.

Explain the classification using the previously approved behaviour in plain
language. If the client's request is unclear, clarify whether the software fails
to perform that behaviour or the desired behaviour has changed. Keep requirement
exploration within Phase 1 of the cycle that will address the change.

After recording a requirement change or addition, ask for acceptance of the
current software, for example:
"I've recorded that request for the next cycle. The software implements the
behaviour we approved, and its verification is complete. Do you accept this
software and agree to complete this cycle?"

Wait for the client's explicit acceptance. A request recorded for a later cycle
does not itself constitute acceptance of the current software.

---

## Transition to idle

When acceptance confirmation is complete, switch to the idle state. In this
experiment, the trial ends after acceptance of the first cycle. Retain requests
for later cycles in the session log.

---

## Session log

On acceptance completion, record the following in the session log:
- List of accepted scenarios
- Cycle number
- Acceptance result (approved / partially approved / rejected)
- Requirement changes or additions recorded for a later cycle

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop — additional management features]
- Approved scenarios: [12]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

#!/usr/bin/env python """Gherkin-based acceptance tests: drive the real UI in a browser against a local fixture site. Starts the fixture server and the app server, runs the checks, and tears everything down. Exit code 0 = all scenarios passed.""" import os, sys, socket, subprocess, tempfile, time, urllib.request, pathlib from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] def free_port(): s = socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)); p = s.getsockname()[1]; s.close(); return p def wait_http(url, timeout=15): end = time.time() + timeout while time.time() < end: try: urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=1); return True except Exception: time.sleep(0.2) return False FIX = free_port(); APP = free_port() DATA = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='bm-accept-') FIXBASE = f'http://127.0.0.1:{FIX}' APPBASE = f'http://127.0.0.1:{APP}' fixture = subprocess.Popen(['node', 'test/fixture-server.js'], cwd=ROOT, env={**os.environ, 'PORT': str(FIX)}) app = subprocess.Popen(['node', 'src/server.js'], cwd=ROOT, env={**os.environ, 'PORT': str(APP), 'HOST': '127.0.0.1', 'DATA_DIR': DATA, 'ARCHIVE_BASE': FIXBASE}) passed = 0 failed = [] def check(name, cond): global passed if cond: passed += 1; print(f' ✓ {name}') else: failed.append(name); print(f' ✗ {name}') try: assert wait_http(FIXBASE + '/img.png'), 'fixture did not start' assert wait_http(APPBASE + '/api/state'), 'app did not start' with sync_playwright() as pw: b = pw.chromium.launch() page = pw.chromium.launch().new_page(viewport={'width': 1000, 'height': 1200}) errors = [] page.on('pageerror', lambda e: errors.append(str(e))) page.on('console', lambda m: errors.append(m.text) if m.type == 'error' else None) page.goto(APPBASE) page.wait_for_selector('[data-harness-ready="true"]') def save(url, note=None, tags=None): page.fill('#url', url) if tags: for t in tags: inp = page.query_selector('#saveTags .tag-entry'); inp.fill(t); inp.press('Enter') if note is not None: page.fill('#saveNote', note) page.click('#saveBtn') page.wait_for_timeout(500) def titles(): return page.eval_on_selector_all('.card .title, .card .title-input', 'els=>els.map(e=>e.textContent||e.value)') # SCN-001 save + auto details save(FIXBASE + '/page', note='**why** saved', tags=['dev']) check('SCN-001 saved with auto title', any('Sample Page 1' in t for t in titles())) check('SCN-001 preview image present', page.eval_on_selector_all('.card .thumb img', 'e=>e.length') >= 1) check('SCN-025 note renders markdown (strong)', page.query_selector('.card .note strong') is not None) check('SCN-002 tag chip shown', page.eval_on_selector_all('.card .chip', 'e=>e.some(x=>x.textContent.includes("dev"))')) # SCN-008 invalid page.fill('#url', 'notalink'); page.click('#saveBtn'); page.wait_for_timeout(200) check('SCN-008 invalid link message', 'look like a link' in (page.inner_text('#saveMsg') or '')) # SCN-009 duplicate -> edit existing save(FIXBASE + '/page') check('SCN-009 duplicate warns', 'already saved' in (page.inner_text('#saveMsg') or '')) page.click('#gotoDup'); page.wait_for_timeout(300) check('SCN-009 opens existing in edit', page.query_selector('.card .title-input') is not None) # cancel edit by pressing Done (title unchanged) page.eval_on_selector_all('.card .primary-btn', 'els=>{const b=els.find(x=>x.textContent==="Done"); if(b) b.click();}'); page.wait_for_timeout(300) # SCN-010 unreadable page saves + edit fields save(FIXBASE + '/fail') check('SCN-010 unreadable saved in edit mode', page.query_selector('.card .title-input') is not None) page.eval_on_selector('.card .title-input', 'e=>e.value="Manual title"') page.fill('.card .title-input', 'Manual title') page.eval_on_selector_all('.card .primary-btn', 'els=>{const b=els.find(x=>x.textContent==="Done"); b.click();}'); page.wait_for_timeout(300) check('SCN-010 manual title saved', any('Manual title' in t for t in titles())) # SCN-007 search page.fill('#search', '"sample page 1"'); page.wait_for_timeout(200) check('SCN-007 phrase search', any('Sample Page 1' in t for t in titles()) and len([t for t in titles() if 'Sample' in t]) == 1) page.fill('#search', '#dev'); # Design decisions — Cycle 1

Production implementation of the bookmark manager. Built fresh from the approved
scenarios' GWT (SCN-001…025); no prototype code was reused.

## Architecture

- **Zero runtime dependencies.** Node's built-in `http` serves both the static
  frontend and a small JSON API. Chosen over Express/frameworks to keep the
  install/lockfile trivial and the app robust offline. Alternative dropped:
  Express + SQLite (heavier, native build risk) — unnecessary for a single user.
- **Storage: one JSON document** (`data/db.json`) mutated synchronously with an
  atomic tmp-write+rename. Adequate and simple for a personal single-user app.
  Snapshots are stored as files under `data/snapshots/`. `DATA_DIR` env overrides
  the location (used by tests for isolation).
- **Client-side search / filter / sort / pagination.** The full library loads
  once (`GET /api/state`); the browser does querying and paging for snappy,
  offline-friendly interaction. The server's real jobs are persistence and the
  network-bound operations the browser cannot do (metadata, snapshots, archive).
- **Shared modules** (`src/query.js`, `src/markdown.js`, `src/importexport.js`)
  are UMD-style so the exact same code runs in Node unit tests and in the browser
  (served under `/lib/*`). This keeps the search grammar, Markdown renderer, and
  bookmarks-file parser single-sourced and testable.

## Notable choices

- **Search grammar** (SCN-007): tokenizer + recursive-descent parser supporting
  quoted phrases, `#tag`, `AND/OR/NOT`, parentheses and implicit AND. Malformed
  queries never throw — they fall back to a plain-text match (`ok:false`) so live
  typing degrades gracefully. Highlighting uses one combined regex pass to avoid
  re-matching inside inserted `<mark>` tags.
- **Markdown notes** (SCN-025): HTML is escaped first; only a safe subset is then
  re-introduced; only `http/https` links become anchors. Raw HTML is shown as
  text, never executed.
- **Duplicate key** (SCN-009): `host (minus www.) + path (no trailing slash) +
  query`, lower-cased. Case, `www.` and trailing slash are ignored; query strings
  distinguish URLs (a deliberate correction found during testing).
- **Metadata / snapshot / archive** (SCN-001/010/019/020): all network-bound and
  time-bounded. Failures return `{ok:false}` so the bookmark is still saved
  (SCN-010) or the copy/archive is simply reported as failed and retryable. The
  Internet Archive base is `ARCHIVE_BASE`-configurable for testing.
- **Snapshot** stores a self-contained `.html` (stylesheets and images inlined as
  data URIs) or the original `.pdf` bytes unchanged.
- **Undo** (SCN-013/017): delete returns the removed record(s) with their index;
  a `restore` endpoint re-inserts them. The UI shows the undo bar; after it
  elapses the deletion is permanent.

## Ports / runtime

- Application listens on `0.0.0.0:4000` (`npm start`). `PORT`/`HOST` env override.
- `data-harness-ready="true"` is set on `<body>` after initial state loads.

## Testing

- Unit/integration: `node --test test/unit/*.test.js` (query, markdown,
  import/export, and the full service against a local fixture site).
- Gherkin acceptance: `python test/acceptance/acceptance.py` starts the fixture
  site + app and drives the real UI through every scenario.

# Design decisions — Cycle 1

Production implementation of the bookmark manager. Built fresh from the approved
scenarios' GWT (SCN-001…025); no prototype code was reused.

## Architecture

- **Zero runtime dependencies.** Node's built-in `http` serves both the static
  frontend and a small JSON API. Chosen over Express/frameworks to keep the
  install/lockfile trivial and the app robust offline. Alternative dropped:
  Express + SQLite (heavier, native build risk) — unnecessary for a single user.
- **Storage: one JSON document** (`data/db.json`) mutated synchronously with an
  atomic tmp-write+rename. Adequate and simple for a personal single-user app.
  Snapshots are stored as files under `data/snapshots/`. `DATA_DIR` env overrides
  the location (used by tests for isolation).
- **Client-side search / filter / sort / pagination.** The full library loads
  once (`GET /api/state`); the browser does querying and paging for snappy,
  offline-friendly interaction. The server's real jobs are persistence and the
  network-bound operations the browser cannot do (metadata, snapshots, archive).
- **Shared modules** (`src/query.js`, `src/markdown.js`, `src/importexport.js`)
  are UMD-style so the exact same code runs in Node unit tests and in the browser
  (served under `/lib/*`). This keeps the search grammar, Markdown renderer, and
  bookmarks-file parser single-sourced and testable.

## Notable choices

- **Search grammar** (SCN-007): tokenizer + recursive-descent parser supporting
  quoted phrases, `#tag`, `AND/OR/NOT`, parentheses and implicit AND. Malformed
  queries never throw — they fall back to a plain-text match (`ok:false`) so live
  typing degrades gracefully. Highlighting uses one combined regex pass to avoid
  re-matching inside inserted `<mark>` tags.
- **Markdown notes** (SCN-025): HTML is escaped first; only a safe subset is then
  re-introduced; only `http/https` links become anchors. Raw HTML is shown as
  text, never executed.
- **Duplicate key** (SCN-009): `host (minus www.) + path (no trailing slash) +
  query`, lower-cased. Case, `www.` and trailing slash are ignored; query strings
  distinguish URLs (a deliberate correction found during testing).
- **Metadata / snapshot / archive** (SCN-001/010/019/020): all network-bound and
  time-bounded. Failures return `{ok:false}` so the bookmark is still saved
  (SCN-010) or the copy/archive is simply reported as failed and retryable. The
  Internet Archive base is `ARCHIVE_BASE`-configurable for testing.
- **Snapshot** stores a self-contained `.html` (stylesheets and images inlined as
  data URIs) or the original `.pdf` bytes unchanged.
- **Undo** (SCN-013/017): delete returns the removed record(s) with their index;
  a `restore` endpoint re-inserts them. The UI shows the undo bar; after it
  elapses the deletion is permanent.

## Ports / runtime

- Application listens on `0.0.0.0:4000` (`npm start`). `PORT`/`HOST` env override.
- `data-harness-ready="true"` is set on `<body>` after initial state loads.

## Testing

- Unit/integration: `node --test test/unit/*.test.js` (query, markdown,
  import/export, and the full service against a local fixture site).
- Gherkin acceptance: `python test/acceptance/acceptance.py` starts the fixture
  site + app and drives the real UI through every scenario.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 2]
- Current step: [Development]
- Approved scenarios: [25]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

The build is complete and verified. Here's the acceptance report.

## Your bookmark manager is built and ready to review

**Open it at:** http://maker:4000 — it starts on a clean, empty library (your real first-run), and since it's a live app you can paste in real links and watch the details fill in automatically.

### What was built
Everything we agreed, implemented fresh from the behaviours you approved (25 scenarios) — saving with automatic details, tags & Markdown notes, editing everything later, read-later/archive, powerful search + tag filter + saved searches, sorting, bulk actions, full-page & PDF copies plus Internet Archive, browser import/export, display preferences with paging, and all the empty/error/duplicate/overflow cases.

### Verification — passed
- **Behaviour (acceptance) tests: 35/35 passed.** An automated browser drives the real app through every approved scenario — saving, the duplicate-and-edit flow, the unreadable-page fallback, the full search grammar (phrases, `#tag`, AND/OR/NOT, graceful fallback), read-later/archive, delete-with-undo, bulk actions, snapshots, Internet Archive, import (preserving titles/dates/tags), export, preferences and paging.
- **Internal tests: 34/34 passed.** Covering the search engine, Markdown renderer, import/export, and all the data operations against a controlled test site.
- **Live check:** a real save of a public page fetched its title correctly, with no errors.
- During testing I found and fixed two genuine defects: duplicate-detection was ignoring query strings, and the search highlighter mis-handled single-letter terms — both corrected and re-verified.

A couple of honesty notes: the automatic details, page snapshots, and Internet Archive step reach out to the live internet, so their results depend on the target site and that service being reachable; when something can't be fetched, the app saves the link anyway and lets you retry, exactly as we agreed.

**Do you accept this software as the completion of this cycle, on the basis of the behaviour we approved and the verification above?** If anything doesn't match what we approved, tell me and I'll correct it within this cycle; anything that would change or extend an approved behaviour I'll record for a future cycle.
